activePlan.objective: Add a local pre-push Git hook enforcing The Crucible's own fast verification set, so a red push never leaves the machine, mirroring a fix the owner shared from another repository where a non-executable tracked hook silently skipped its check.
steps: Confirm this repository has no existing .githooks setup (it did not) before adding one.
Add .githooks/pre-push running the fast offline checks: lint:workflows, docs:check, test, validate, audit:clutter, audit:privacy, audit:security.
Add src/installGitHooks.js to chmod the hook executable and set core.hooksPath, wired into the standard npm "prepare" lifecycle so a lost executable bit self-heals on the next install.
Verify live: staged the hook, confirmed Git tracks it as mode 100755, and ran it end-to-end against this real repository.

completed: Added .githooks/pre-push and src/installGitHooks.js, wired via package.json's "prepare" script.
Added test/installGitHooks.test.js (self-heal, no-op without .githooks, fails closed if Git is unavailable) and a workflow.test.js check that the hook stays tracked at mode 100755.
Documented the hook in AGENTS.md's "CI on development" section.
Ran the hook itself end-to-end against this repository, not just its component npm scripts individually.
verification: lint:workflows, docs:check, validate, audit:clutter, audit:privacy, and audit:security all pass against the current staged snapshot.
git ls-files -s .githooks/pre-push confirms mode 100755 in the index, not just on disk.
Ran `node src/installGitHooks.js && sh .githooks/pre-push` directly and it completed successfully end-to-end.
remaining: Commit and push to development, then verify AI handoff policy, AI conflict governance, Self-Test, and CodeQL for the exact commit.
No default-branch or repository-setting change involved; nothing further requires owner authorization.
